36 The diagram shows four identical resistors connected in a circuit.
Which resistor dissipates the most power?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice that resistor A is in the main line from the cell, while the circuit then splits into a B-C series branch in parallel with D.
Recall that for identical resistors power $P = I^2R$ is largest where the current $I$ is largest.
Compare the total current through A with the smaller split currents through B and C together and through D alone.
walkthrough: Trace the circuit from the cell: current passes down through A to the lower left junction, then divides into the B-C path and the D path before rejoining to the cell.
All four resistors have the same resistance $R$, so power $P = I^2R$ depends only on the current $I$ in each resistor.
Let the total current be $I$. Resistor A carries all of $I$, while the current splits so B and C each carry $I_1$ and D carries $I_2$, with $I = I_1 + I_2$.
Therefore $I$ in A is greater than $I_1$ in B and C and greater than $I_2$ in D.
Since $P$ increases with $I^2$, the largest current gives the largest dissipation. This is option A.

A.explanation: Resistor A carries the total current from the cell before it splits, so with $P = I^2R$ and identical $R$ it has the largest $I$ and most power.

B.explanation: Resistor B carries only part of the total current because it is in series with C in one of two parallel branches.

C.explanation: Resistor C carries the same reduced current as B, so its $I^2R$ power is less than for the resistor carrying the full current.

D.explanation: Resistor D carries only one part of the split current in parallel with the B-C branch, so its current and power are smaller.
